tutorial.step1.title: Log in with Discord
tutorial.step1.p1: Click {{b}}"Login with Discord"{{bEnd}} on the home page. This creates your account using your Discord identity.
tutorial.step1.p2: You'll be redirected to Discord to authorize. The bot only reads your username and avatar.
tutorial.step1.tip1: Click {{b}}"Authorize"{{bEnd}} to continue. No special permissions are needed — the bot only reads your public profile.
tutorial.step1.alt1: Atleta home page with Get Started with Discord button
tutorial.step2.title: Link Your Twitch Account (Optional)
tutorial.step2.p1: From the dashboard, click {{b}}"Link Twitch Account"{{bEnd}} if you want to enable subscriber role sync for your own channel. This step is optional — you can watch any Twitch channel without linking.
tutorial.step3.title: Add the Bot to Your Discord Server
tutorial.step3.p1: Click {{b}}"+ Add Bot to Server"{{bEnd}} from the dashboard. This opens Discord's authorization page in a new tab.
tutorial.step3.p2: Select which server you want to add the bot to and click {{b}}"Continue"{{bEnd}}.
tutorial.step3.li1: You need {{b}}Manage Server{{bEnd}} permission in the Discord server
tutorial.step3.li2: The bot will request permissions to send messages, embed links, and manage roles
tutorial.step3.li3: After authorizing, go back to the dashboard
tutorial.step3.alt1: Dashboard with Add Bot to Server button
tutorial.step3.alt2: Discord — Select a server to add the bot
tutorial.step4.title: Claim Your Server
tutorial.step4.p1: After adding the bot, your server will appear under {{b}}"Available Servers"{{bEnd}} on the dashboard. Click {{b}}"Claim"{{bEnd}} to link it to your account.
tutorial.step4.p2: Once claimed, you'll see the server settings page where you can configure welcome messages, subscriber role sync, and more.
tutorial.step4.tip1: Each server can only be claimed by one user. If someone else has already set up the bot on that server, you won't see it in the list.
tutorial.step4.alt1: Dashboard showing Available Servers with Claim button
tutorial.step4.alt2: Server settings page with Twitch Channels and YouTube Channels buttons
tutorial.step4.alt2NoYoutube: Server settings page with the Twitch Channels button
tutorial.step5.title: Add Twitch Channels to Watch
tutorial.step5.p1: Click the {{b}}"Twitch Channels"{{bEnd}} button on your server to manage which Twitch streamers you want notifications for.
tutorial.step5.p2: You'll see the Twitch Channels page. Enter any Twitch username and choose which Discord channels should receive live and clip notifications.
tutorial.step5.p3: Fill in a Twitch username and select the notification channels. You can set different Discord channels for live alerts and clips, or leave one disabled.
tutorial.step5.p4: Click {{b}}"Add Channel"{{bEnd}} and you're done! The channel will appear in your watched list and notifications will start within a minute.
tutorial.step5.alt1: Server settings showing Twitch Channels and YouTube Channels buttons
tutorial.step5.alt1NoYoutube: Server settings showing the Twitch Channels button
tutorial.step5.alt2: Twitch Channels page — empty state with add form
tutorial.step5.alt3: Filling in a Twitch username with notification channels selected
tutorial.step5.alt4: Channel added successfully with watched channels list showing
tutorial.step6.title: Add YouTube Channels (Optional)
tutorial.step6.p1: Click the {{b}}"YouTube"{{bEnd}} tab on your server settings to add YouTube channels. You can enter a {{b}}@username{{bEnd}} or {{b}}Channel ID{{bEnd}} (starts with {{c}}UC{{cEnd}}).
tutorial.step6.p2: Choose which Discord channels should receive {{b}}video/shorts notifications{{bEnd}} and {{b}}live notifications{{bEnd}}, then click {{b}}"Add Channel"{{bEnd}}.
tutorial.step6.tip1: Video/shorts notifications use the free YouTube RSS feed and don't need an API key. Live detection requires a YouTube Data API key.
tutorial.step6.alt1: YouTube tab — Add a YouTube channel form
tutorial.step6.alt2: YouTube channel added to watched list
tutorial.step7.title: Configure Welcome Messages (Optional)
tutorial.step7.p1: In your server {{b}}"Settings"{{bEnd}} page, enable the welcome message feature:
tutorial.step7.li2: Select which channel to send welcome messages to
tutorial.step7.li3: Optionally write a custom welcome message
tutorial.step7.alt1: Server Settings showing Welcome Message configuration
tutorial.step8.title: Enable Subscriber Role Sync (Optional)
tutorial.step8.p1: This feature automatically gives a Discord role to your Twitch subscribers:
tutorial.step8.p2: {{b}}1.{{bEnd}} First, link your Twitch account and click {{b}}"Enable Sub Sync"{{bEnd}} from the dashboard — this authorizes the bot to read your subscriber list.
tutorial.step8.p3: {{b}}2.{{bEnd}} In your Discord server, go to {{b}}Server Settings → Roles → Atleta{{bEnd}} and make sure the {{b}}Administrator{{bEnd}} permission is enabled.
tutorial.step8.p4: {{b}}3.{{bEnd}} Make sure the {{b}}Atleta role is above{{bEnd}} the subscriber role in the roles list. If it's not, drag it above — the bot can only assign roles lower than its own.
tutorial.step8.p5: {{b}}4.{{bEnd}} In the Atleta dashboard, go to your server {{b}}Settings{{bEnd}}, toggle on {{b}}Subscriber Role Sync{{bEnd}} and select the role. Your community members type {{c}}/link{{cEnd}} in Discord to connect their Twitch account.
tutorial.step8.tip1: The bot checks every 10 minutes and assigns or removes the role automatically. Subscribers need to use {{c}}/link{{cEnd}} once to connect their Twitch and Discord accounts.
tutorial.step8.alt1: Dashboard showing Enable Sub Sync button
tutorial.step8.alt2: Atleta role with Administrator permission enabled
tutorial.step8.alt3: Atleta role positioned above Sub Role in the roles list
tutorial.step8.alt4: Discord showing /link command in a channel

multistream.regenerate.hint: Use this if your stream key was shared or leaked. The old key stops working at once.
multistream.regenerate.confirm: Make a new stream key? The current key stops working immediately: OBS cannot stream through the relay until you paste the new key into OBS (Settings > Stream > Stream Key).
multistream.regenerate.done: New stream key made. Paste it into OBS (Settings > Stream > Stream Key) before you go live again.

multistream.regenerate.refusedUnknown: The relay did not answer, so it is not clear whether you are live. Try again in a minute.
